bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties
bookInfo.author: Ouyang Xiu

title.zh: 卷十二 周本紀第十二: 世宗 恭帝
title.en: Volume 12 Later Zhou Annals 3: Shizong, Emperor Gong
title.raw: 卷十二 周本紀第十二: 世宗 恭帝 Volume 12 Later Zhou Annals 3: Shizong, Emperor Gong

sentences.zh: 卷十二 周本纪第十二

translations.literal: Volume Twelve. Annals of Zhou, Chapter Twelve
translations.idiomatic: Volume 12 — Annals of Zhou, Chapter 12

sentences.zh: 世宗睿武孝文皇帝，本姓柴氏，邢州龙冈人也。

translations.literal: Shizong, the Sagacious Martial Filial Civil Emperor—original surname Chai, a native of Longgang in Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong, temple name the Sagacious Martial Filial Civil Emperor, was born of the Chai clan at Longgang in Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 柴氏女适太祖，是为圣穆皇 后。

translations.literal: A daughter of the Chai clan married Taizu; she became Empress Shengmu.
translations.idiomatic: A Chai clanswoman wed Taizu and was enthroned as Empress Shengmu.

sentences.zh: 后兄守礼子荣，幼从姑长太祖家，以谨厚见爱，太祖遂以为子。

translations.literal: Rong, son of the empress’s brother Shouli, in youth followed his aunt who had grown up in Taizu’s household; for his careful steadiness he was beloved, and Taizu thus made him his son.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, Shouli’s son and the empress’s nephew, was raised from boyhood in Taizu’s house through his aunt; his sober loyalty won affection, and Taizu adopted him as a son.

sentences.zh: 太祖后稍贵， 荣亦壮，而器貌英奇，善骑射，略通书史黄老，性沈重寡言。

translations.literal: After Taizu later rose somewhat in rank, Rong also came of age; his bearing and appearance were heroic and striking, he was skilled at mounted archery, had slight knowledge of texts, histories, and Yellow Emperor–Laozi learning, and by nature was grave and sparing of words.
translations.idiomatic: As Taizu’s star rose, Rong matured into a man of striking looks and presence, expert in the saddle and bow, with a modest grounding in the classics, histories, and Daoist texts, and a temperament grave and quiet.

sentences.zh: 太祖为汉枢密使， 荣为左监门卫大将军。

translations.literal: When Taizu was Han’s privy commissioner, Rong was Grand General of the Left Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: While Taizu served Later Han as privy commissioner, Rong held the post of Grand General of the Left Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 太祖镇天雄，荣领贵州刺史、天雄军牙内都指挥使。

translations.literal: When Taizu garrisoned Tianxiong, Rong held the posts of prefect of Guizhou and commander-in-chief of the Tianxiong army’s inner guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took command at Tianxiong, Rong became prefect of Guizhou and commander-in-chief of the Tianxiong inner guard.

sentences.zh: 乾祐三年冬，周兵起魏，犯京师，留荣守魏。

translations.literal: In winter of Qianyou 3, Zhou troops rose in Wei and marched on the capital; Rong was left to hold Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Qianyou 3 the Zhou army rose in Wei and struck for the capital; Rong stayed behind to guard Wei.

sentences.zh: 太祖入立，拜澶州刺史、镇宁 军节度使，检校太傅、同中书门下平章事。

translations.literal: When Taizu entered and took the throne, Rong was appointed prefect of Cao, military commissioner of Zhenning, honorary grand tutor, and associate grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu seized the throne, Rong was made prefect of Cao, military commissioner of Zhenning, honorary grand tutor, and associate grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 荣素为枢密使王峻所忌，广顺三年正 月来朝，不得留。

translations.literal: Rong had long been envied by Privy Commissioner Wang Jun; in the first month of Guangshun 3 he came to court and was not permitted to stay.
translations.idiomatic: Privy Commissioner Wang Jun had long resented Rong; when Rong came to court in the first month of Guangshun 3, he was sent back and not allowed to remain.

sentences.zh: 既而峻有罪诛，三月，拜荣开封尹，封晋王。

translations.literal: Before long Jun was guilty and executed; in the third month Rong was appointed Mayor of the Eastern Capital and enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was soon condemned and put to death; in the third month Rong became Mayor of the Eastern Capital and Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 是冬，卜以来年 正月朔旦有事于南郊，而太祖遇疾，不能视朝者久之。

translations.literal: That winter they divined to perform the southern suburb rite at dawn on the new year of the coming year; but Taizu fell ill and for a long time could not hold court.
translations.idiomatic: That winter auguries fixed the southern suburb rite for dawn on the coming new year, yet Taizu fell ill and went long without holding court.

sentences.zh: 显德元年正月丙子，郊，仅而成礼，即以王判内外兵马事。

translations.literal: On bingzi in the first month of Xiande 1 the suburb rite was performed and barely completed; the Prince was then appointed to judge inner and outer military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi in the first month of Xiande 1 the suburban sacrifice was rushed through; the Prince of Jin was then put in charge of all military affairs within and without.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，太祖崩， 秘不发丧。

translations.literal: On renchen Taizu died; the death was kept secret and mourning not announced.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Taizu died; the court concealed the death and withheld the mourning proclamation.

sentences.zh: 丙申，发丧，皇帝即位于柩前。

translations.literal: On bingshen mourning was announced and the emperor acceded before the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the mourning was proclaimed and the new emperor took the throne before the bier.

sentences.zh: 右监门卫大将军魏仁浦为枢密副使。

translations.literal: Wei Renpu, Grand General of the Right Gate Guard, was made vice privy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Renpu, Grand General of the Right Gate Guard, became vice privy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二月庚戌，回鹘遣使者来。

translations.literal: On gengxu in the second month the Uyghurs sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu in the second month Uyghur envoys arrived.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，冯道为大行皇帝山陵使，太常卿田敏为礼仪使， 兵部尚书张昭为卤簿使，御史中丞张煦为仪仗使，开封少尹权判府事王敏为桥道 顿递使。

translations.literal: On dingmao Feng Dao was made commissioner for the late emperor’s mausoleum, Minister of Rites Tian Min commissioner of ritual, Minister of War Zhang Zhao commissioner of insignia, Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhang Xu commissioner of ceremonial guards, and Junior Mayor of Kaifeng Wang Min, acting mayor, commissioner of bridges, roads, and relay stations.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Feng Dao was named mausoleum commissioner for the late emperor; Tian Min, Minister of Rites, oversaw ritual; Zhang Zhao, Minister of War, insignia; Zhang Xu, Vice Censor-in-Chief, ceremonial guards; and Wang Min, junior mayor of Kaifeng acting as mayor, bridges, roads, and relays.

sentences.zh: 汉人来讨，攻自潞州。

translations.literal: The Han came to attack, pressing from Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Han forces marched to punish Zhou, advancing from Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月辛巳，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinsi in the third month, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi in the third month a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 癸未，郑仁诲留守东京。

translations.literal: On guimao Zheng Renhui was left to guard the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Zheng Renhui was posted to guard the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 乙酉， 如潞州以攻汉。

translations.literal: On yiyou the emperor went to Luzhou to attack Han.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou the emperor marched on Luzhou against Northern Han.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，次泽州，阅兵于北郊。

translations.literal: On renchen he halted at Ze Prefecture and reviewed troops at the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen he stopped at Ze Prefecture and held a military review north of the city.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，及刘旻战于高原，败之，追 及于高平，又败之。

translations.literal: On guisi he fought Liu Chong on the high plain, defeated him, pursued to Gaoping, and defeated him again.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi he met Liu Chong on the high plain, routed him, chased him to Gaoping, and routed him again.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，幸潞州。

translations.literal: On dingyou he visited Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou he went in person to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 己亥，侍卫马军都指挥使樊爱能、步军都指 挥使何徽伏诛。

translations.literal: On jihai Fan Aineng, commander-in-chief of the palace horse guard, and He Hui, commander-in-chief of the palace foot guard, were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Fan Aineng, commander of the palace horse guard, and He Hui, commander of the palace foot guard, were put to death.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，天雄军节度使符彦卿为河东行营都部署。

translations.literal: On renyin Fu Yanqing, military commissioner of the Tianxiong army, was made overall commander of the eastern campaign against Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Fu Yanqing, military commissioner of Tianxiong, was appointed overall commander of the Hedong campaign.

sentences.zh: 夏四月乙卯，葬 神圣文武恭肃孝皇帝于嵩陵。

translations.literal: On yimao in the fourth month of summer the Sagely, Divine, Martial, Civil, Reverent, Filial Emperor was buried at Songling.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao in the fourth month Taizu, the Sagely, Divine, Martial, Civil, Reverent, Filial Emperor, was interred at Songling.

sentences.zh: 汾州防御使董希颜叛于汉来附。

translations.literal: Dong Xiyan, defense commissioner of Fen Prefecture, rebelled against Han and came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xiyan, defense commissioner of Fen Prefecture, broke with Northern Han and defected to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，辽州刺史张 汉超叛于汉来附。

translations.literal: On bingchen Zhang Hanchao, prefect of Liao Prefecture, rebelled against Han and came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Liao Prefecture prefect Zhang Hanchao rebelled against Northern Han and submitted to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，取岚、宪州。

translations.literal: On xinyou Lan and Xian prefectures were taken.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Lan and Xian prefectures fell.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，立卫国夫人符氏为皇后。

translations.literal: On renxu Lady Fu of the Wei state was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Lady Fu of Wei was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 取石、泌 州。

translations.literal: Shi and Bi prefectures were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Shi and Bi prefectures were captured.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，冯道薨。

translations.literal: On yichou Feng Dao died.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Feng Dao died.

sentences.zh: 庚午，赦潞州流罪以下囚。

translations.literal: On gengwu prisoners in Luzhou guilty of exile or less were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Luzhou prisoners sentenced to exile or below were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 如太原。

translations.literal: The emperor went to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marched on Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 忻州监军李勍杀其刺史 赵皋，叛于汉来附。

translations.literal: Li Qiong, military supervisor of Xin Prefecture, killed its prefect Zhao Gao, rebelled against Han, and came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiong, Xin Prefecture’s military supervisor, killed Prefect Zhao Gao, turned on Northern Han, and defected to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 五月丙子，代州守将郑处谦叛于汉来附，契丹救汉。

translations.literal: On bingzi in the fifth month Zheng Chuqian, garrison commander of Dai Prefecture, rebelled against Han and came to submit; the Khitan came to rescue Han.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi in the fifth month Dai’s garrison commander Zheng Chuqian rebelled against Northern Han and submitted; the Khitan marched to relieve Han.

sentences.zh: 丁酉， 回鹘使因难敌略来。

translations.literal: On dingyou the Uyghur envoy Yinandielue came.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the Uyghur envoy Yinandielue arrived.

sentences.zh: 符彦卿及契丹战于忻口，败绩，先锋都指挥使史彦超死之。

translations.literal: Fu Yanqing fought the Khitan at Xinkou and was defeated; Vanguard Commander Shi Yanchao died in the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanqing met the Khitan at Xinkou and was beaten; Vanguard Commander Shi Yanchao fell in the fight.

sentences.zh: 六月乙巳，班师。

translations.literal: On yisi in the sixth month the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi in the sixth month the army marched home.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，次新郑，前拜嵩陵。

translations.literal: On yichou he halted at Xinzheng and went first to pay respects at Songling.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou he stopped at Xinzheng and visited Songling to mourn Taizu.

sentences.zh: 庚午，至自太原。

translations.literal: On gengwu he returned from Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu he came back from the Taiyuan campaign.

sentences.zh: 秋七月庚辰，阅 稼于南御庄。

translations.literal: On gengchen in the seventh month of autumn he inspected the crops at the Southern Imperial Estate.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen in the seventh month he inspected the harvest at the Southern Imperial Farm.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，枢密院直学士、工部侍郎景范为中书侍郎、同中书门下平章 事，魏仁浦为枢密使。

translations.literal: On guisi Jing Fan, academician of the Privy Council and vice minister of works, was made vice director of the Secretariat and associate grand councilor; Wei Renpu was made privy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Privy Council academician and Vice Minister of Works Jing Fan became vice director of the Secretariat and associate grand councilor; Wei Renpu was named privy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 冬十月甲辰，杀左羽林大将军孟汉卿。

translations.literal: On jiachen in the tenth month of winter Meng Hanqing, Grand General of the Left Feathered Forest, was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen in the tenth month Meng Hanqing, Grand General of the Left Feathered Forest, was put to death.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月，增筑京城。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the third year the capital walls were enlarged.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Xiande 3 the capital fortifications were extended.

sentences.zh: 庚子，向训留守东京。

translations.literal: On gengzi Xiang Xun was left to guard the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Xiang Xun was posted to guard the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，南征。

translations.literal: On renyin the southern campaign began.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the emperor launched the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，侍卫亲 军都指挥使李重进及唐人战于正阳，败之。

translations.literal: On xinhai Li Chongjin, commander-in-chief of the palace personal guard, fought the Tang at Zhengyang and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Li Chongjin, commander of the palace personal guard, met Southern Tang forces at Zhengyang and routed them.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，重进为淮南道行营都招讨使。

translations.literal: On jiayin Chongjin was made overall commander and recruiter for the Huainan circuit campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Li Chongjin was appointed overall commander of the Huainan campaign.

sentences.zh: 二月丙寅，幸下蔡浮桥。

translations.literal: On bingyin in the second month the emperor visited the pontoon bridge at Xiacai.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin in the second month he inspected the floating bridge at Xiacai.

sentences.zh: 壬申，克滁州。

translations.literal: On renshen Chu Prefecture was taken.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Chu Prefecture fell.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，李景来求成，不答。

translations.literal: On jiaxu Li Jing came to sue for peace; no answer was given.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Li Jing of Southern Tang sued for peace; the court gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 壬午，景使 其臣钟谟来奉表。

translations.literal: On renwu Jing sent his minister Zhong Mo to present a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Li Jing sent his minister Zhong Mo with a formal petition.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，取扬州。

translations.literal: On bingxu Yang Prefecture was taken.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Yang Prefecture was captured.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，取泰州。

translations.literal: On xinmao Tai Prefecture was taken.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Tai Prefecture fell.

sentences.zh: 三月庚子，内外马步军都军头 袁彦为竹龙都部署。

translations.literal: On gengzi Yuan Yan, head of the inner and outer horse and foot armies, was made overall commander of the bamboo-dragon formation.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Yuan Yan, chief of the inner and outer horse and foot forces, was named commander of the bamboo-dragon formation.

sentences.zh: 是月，取光、舒、常州。

translations.literal: That month Guang, Shu, and Chang prefectures were taken.
translations.idiomatic: That month Guang, Shu, and Chang prefectures were captured.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，常、泰州复入于唐。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer Chang and Tai prefectures returned to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Chang and Tai prefectures slipped back to Southern Tang control.

sentences.zh: 五月 乙卯，至自淮南，赦京师囚。

translations.literal: On yimao in the fifth month the emperor returned from Huainan and pardoned prisoners in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao in the fifth month he returned from Huainan and granted amnesty to capital prisoners.

sentences.zh: 六月壬申，德音赦淮南囚。

translations.literal: On renshen in the sixth month a merciful edict pardoned Huainan prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen in the sixth month a lenient edict freed Huainan prisoners.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，皇后崩。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the empress died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the empress died.

sentences.zh: 扬、 光、舒、滁州复入于唐。

translations.literal: Yang, Guang, Shu, and Chu prefectures returned to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang, Guang, Shu, and Chu prefectures reverted to Southern Tang.

sentences.zh: 八月乙丑，课民种禾及韭。

translations.literal: On yichou in the eighth month the people were ordered to plant grain and leeks.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou in the eighth month the court ordered households to plant grain and leeks.

sentences.zh: 九月丙午，端明殿学士、左 散骑常侍王朴为尚书户部侍郎、枢密副使。

translations.literal: On bingwu in the ninth month Wang Pu, academician of the Duanming Hall and left regular attendant, was made vice minister of revenue and vice privy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu in the ninth month Duanming Hall academician and Left Regular Attendant Wang Pu became Vice Minister of Revenue and vice privy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛酉，葬宣懿皇后于懿陵。

translations.literal: On xinyou in the tenth month of winter Empress Xuanyi was buried at Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou in the tenth month Empress Xuanyi was interred at Yiling.

sentences.zh: 十 一月庚寅，废诸祠不在祀典者。

translations.literal: On gengyin in the eleventh month shrines not in the statutory canon of sacrifice were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin in the eleventh month unauthorized local cults were shut down.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，杀李景之臣孙晟。

translations.literal: On yisi Sun Sheng, a minister of Li Jing, was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Sun Sheng, a Southern Tang minister of Li Jing, was put to death.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月己丑朔，赦非死罪囚。

translations.literal: On the new-year day jichou in the first month of spring in the fourth year, prisoners not guilty of capital crimes were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: On the new-year day jichou in the first month of Xiande 4, all prisoners short of capital crimes were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 二月甲戌，王朴留守东京。

translations.literal: On jiaxu in the second month Wang Pu was left to guard the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu in the second month Wang Pu was posted to guard the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，南征。

translations.literal: On yihai the southern campaign began.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the emperor launched the southern campaign again.

sentences.zh: 三月丁未，克寿州。

translations.literal: On dingwei in the third month Shou Prefecture was taken.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei in the third month Shou Prefecture fell.

sentences.zh: 夏四月己巳，至自寿州。

translations.literal: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the emperor returned from Shou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi in the fourth month he returned from the Shouzhou campaign.

sentences.zh: 己卯，放降卒八百归于蜀。

translations.literal: On jimao eight hundred surrendered soldiers were released to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao eight hundred captives were sent home to Shu.

sentences.zh: 癸未， 追册彭城郡夫人刘氏为皇后。

translations.literal: On guimao Lady Liu of Pengcheng commandery was posthumously installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Lady Liu of Pengcheng was posthumously enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 五月丙申，杀密州防御使侯希进。

translations.literal: On bingshen in the fifth month Hou Xijin, defense commissioner of Mi Prefecture, was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen in the fifth month Mi Prefecture defense commissioner Hou Xijin was put to death.

sentences.zh: 秋八月乙亥，李 穀罢，王朴为枢密使。

translations.literal: On yihai in the eighth month of autumn Li Gu was dismissed; Wang Pu was made privy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai in the eighth month Li Gu left office and Wang Pu became privy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 癸未，蜀人来归我濮州刺史胡立。

translations.literal: On guimao Shu returned Hu Li, our prefect of Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Shu sent back Hu Li, Zhou’s prefect of Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己巳，王朴留守 东京，三司使张美为大内都点检。

translations.literal: On jisi in the tenth month of winter Wang Pu was left to guard the Eastern Capital; Zhang Mei, commissioner of the three departments, was made chief inspector of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi in the tenth month Wang Pu guarded the Eastern Capital while Zhang Mei, head of the three fiscal departments, was named chief inspector of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 壬申，南征。

translations.literal: On renshen the southern campaign began.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the southern campaign resumed.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙卯，泗州守将范再遇叛 于唐，以其州来降。

translations.literal: On yimao in the twelfth month Fan Zaiyu, garrison commander of Si Prefecture, rebelled against Tang and surrendered the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao in the twelfth month Si Prefecture commander Fan Zaiyu turned on Southern Tang and surrendered his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 庚申，濠州团练使郭廷谓以其州来降。

translations.literal: On gengshen Guo Tingwei, training commissioner of Hao Prefecture, surrendered his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Hao Prefecture training commissioner Guo Tingwei surrendered his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，取泰州。

translations.literal: On dingchou Tai Prefecture was taken.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Tai Prefecture was captured.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月丁亥，取海州。

translations.literal: On dinghai in the first month of spring in the fifth year Hai Prefecture was taken.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai in the first month of Xiande 5 Hai Prefecture fell.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，取静海军。

translations.literal: On renchen the Jinghai army was taken.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the Jinghai command was captured.

sentences.zh: 丁未，克楚州，守将张彦卿、 郑昭业死之。

translations.literal: On dingwei Chu Prefecture was taken; garrison commanders Zhang Yanqing and Zheng Zhaoye died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Chu Prefecture fell; its defenders Zhang Yanqing and Zheng Zhaoye died in the assault.

sentences.zh: 二月甲寅，取雄州。

translations.literal: On jiayin Xiong Prefecture was taken.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Xiong Prefecture was captured.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，如扬州。

translations.literal: On dingmao the emperor went to Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the emperor traveled to Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，如瓜洲。

translations.literal: On guiyou the emperor went to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou he went on to Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 三月壬午朔， 如泰州。

translations.literal: On the new-year day renwu in the third month the emperor went to Tai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the new-year day renwu in the third month he went to Tai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，复如扬州。

translations.literal: On dinghai he returned to Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai he went back to Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，幸迎銮。

translations.literal: On xinmao he visited Yingluan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao he toured Yingluan.

sentences.zh: 己亥，克淮南十有四州，以江为界。

translations.literal: On jihai fourteen Huainan prefectures were taken, with the Yangzi as the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai fourteen Huainan prefectures were secured, the Yangzi River set as the border.

sentences.zh: 三月辛亥，李景来买宴。

translations.literal: On xinhai in the third month Li Jing came to buy a feast.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai in the third month Li Jing came in person to tender submission at a feast.

sentences.zh: 四月庚申，祔五室神主于新庙。

translations.literal: On gengshen in the fourth month the spirit tablets of the five chambers were enshrined in the new temple.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen in the fourth month the five ancestral tablets were installed in the new imperial temple.

sentences.zh: 壬申，至自淮南，回鹘、 达靼遣使者来。

translations.literal: On renshen the emperor returned from Huainan; Uyghur and Tatar envoys came.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen he returned from Huainan; envoys arrived from the Uyghurs and the Tatars.

sentences.zh: 六月辛未，放降卒四千六百于唐。

translations.literal: On xinwei in the sixth month four thousand six hundred surrendered soldiers were released to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei in the sixth month 4,600 captives were sent back to Southern Tang.

sentences.zh: 秋七月乙酉，水部员外郎韩彦 卿市铜于高丽。

translations.literal: On yiyou in the seventh month of autumn Han Yanqing, outer office director of the water ministry, was sent to purchase copper in Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou in the seventh month Han Yanqing of the Water Ministry was dispatched to buy copper in Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，颁《均田图》。

translations.literal: On dinghai the Equal-Field Diagram was promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the court issued the Equal-Field Diagram.

sentences.zh: 九月，占城国王释利因德缦使莆诃散来。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the king of Champa, Shili Yinde Man, sent the envoy Puhesan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the king of Champa, Shili Yinde Man, dispatched the envoy Puhesan.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁酉，括民租。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month on dingyou, the people’s grain rents were levied.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on dingyou in the tenth month, the court levied grain rents from the people.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚戌，作《通礼》、《正乐》。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month on gengxu the Comprehensive Rites and Correct Music were compiled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month on gengxu the court compiled the Comprehensive Rites and the Correct Music.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙戌，罢州 县课户、俸户。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month on bingxu tax-account households and salary households in prefectures and counties were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month on bingxu the court abolished tax-account and salary households in prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 恭皇帝，世宗第四子宗训也。

translations.literal: Emperor Gong was Zongxun, Shizong’s fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gong was Zongxun, the fourth son of Shizong.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，大臣请封皇子为王，世宗谦抑久之。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, his ministers asked that imperial sons be enfeoffed as kings; Shizong declined modestly for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizong’s accession his ministers urged that the princes be enfeoffed as kings, but he long refused out of modest restraint.

sentences.zh: 及北取三关，遇疾还京师，始封宗训梁王，时年七岁。

translations.literal: When he marched north to take the Three Passes he fell ill and returned to the capital; only then was Zongxun enfeoffed as Prince of Liang, aged seven.
translations.idiomatic: When he marched north to recover the Three Passes he fell ill and returned to the capital; only then did he enfeoff Zongxun as Prince of Liang, at the age of seven.

sentences.zh: 七年春正月甲辰，逊于位。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, spring, first month, on jiachen, he abdicated the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the seventh year, on jiachen, he abdicated the throne.

sentences.zh: 宋兴。

translations.literal: The Song arose.
translations.idiomatic: The Song arose.

sentences.zh: 呜呼，五代本纪备矣，君臣之际，可胜道哉！

translations.literal: Alas! The annals of the Five Dynasties are complete—how much can be said of what passed between ruler and subject!
translations.idiomatic: Alas! The annals of the Five Dynasties stand complete—what can fully be told of the bond between ruler and subject!

sentences.zh: 梁之友珪反，唐戕克宁而杀存 乂、从璨，则父子骨肉之恩，几何其不绝矣。

translations.literal: When Liang’s Yougui rebelled, Tang slaughtered Kening and killed Cunyi and Congcan—then how nearly was the bond of father and son, flesh and blood, cut off!
translations.idiomatic: When Liang’s Yougui rebelled, Later Tang slew Kening and put Cunyi and Congcan to death—the tie between father and son, bone and blood, was all but severed.

sentences.zh: 太妃薨而辍朝，立刘氏、冯氏为皇 后，则夫妇之伦几何其不乖而不至于禽兽矣。

translations.literal: When the imperial dowager died they suspended court, yet enthroned Liu and Feng as empresses—then how nearly were the norms of husband and wife overturned short of outright beastliness!
translations.idiomatic: They halted court when the imperial dowager died, yet enthroned Liu and Feng as empresses—the marriage bond was all but wrecked, not far from the conduct of beasts.

sentences.zh: 寒食野祭而焚纸钱，居丧改元而用 乐，杀马延及任圜，则礼乐刑政几何其不坏矣。

translations.literal: Cold Food rites in the wild with paper money burned, changing the era name during mourning while using music, killing Ma Yanji and Ren Yuan—then how nearly were ritual, music, punishments, and governance ruined!
translations.idiomatic: Cold Food sacrifices in the open with spirit money burned, a new reign title proclaimed amid mourning while music played, Ma Yanji and Ren Yuan put to death—ritual, music, punishments, and policy were all but destroyed.

sentences.zh: 至于赛雷山、传箭而扑马，则中 国几何其不夷狄矣。

translations.literal: As for the Thunder-Mountain contest, passing arrows and trampling horses—then how nearly had the Middle Kingdom ceased to be Chinese!
translations.idiomatic: Thunder-Mountain contests, passing the arrow, trampling horses—the Middle Kingdom had all but turned barbarian.

sentences.zh: 可谓乱世也欤！

translations.literal: It may be called an age of chaos indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Truly it may be called an age of chaos!

sentences.zh: 而世宗区区五六年间，取秦陇，平淮右，复 三关，威武之声震慑夷夏，而方内延儒学文章之士，考制度、修《通礼》、定《 正乐》、议《刑统》，其制作之法皆可施于后世。

translations.literal: Yet in a mere five or six years Shizong took Qin and Long, pacified the Huai’s right bank, recovered the Three Passes; his martial renown shook barbarian and Chinese alike, while within the realm he welcomed Confucian scholars, examined institutions, compiled the Comprehensive Rites, fixed the Correct Music, and debated the Penal Code—what he wrought could all be applied in later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in only five or six years Shizong seized Qin and Long, pacified the Huai west, and recovered the Three Passes; his martial fame shook both barbarians and Chinese, while within the realm he gathered Confucian scholars, examined institutions, compiled the Comprehensive Rites, fixed the Correct Music, and debated the Penal Code—institutions fit to govern generations yet unborn.

sentences.zh: 其为人明达英果，论议伟然。

translations.literal: In person he was clear-sighted, resolute, and bold; his counsels were magnanimous.
translations.idiomatic: He was clear-sighted and resolute, bold in counsel and grand in debate.

sentences.zh: 即位之明年，废天下佛寺三千三百三十六。

translations.literal: The year after his accession he abolished 3,336 Buddhist temples throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The year after he took the throne he abolished 3,336 Buddhist temples across the realm.

sentences.zh: 是时中国乏钱，乃诏悉毁天下铜佛像 以铸钱，尝曰：「吾闻佛说以身世为妄，而以利人为急，使其真身尚在，苟利于 世，犹欲割截，况此铜像，岂其所惜哉？

translations.literal: China then lacked coin; an edict ordered all copper Buddha images throughout the realm destroyed to cast cash. He once said: “I have heard that Buddha teaches the bodily world is illusion and that benefiting others is urgent—even if his true body remained, were it useful to the world he would cut it away; how much less these copper images—would he cherish them?
translations.idiomatic: Coin was scarce in China then, and an edict ordered every copper Buddha image in the realm melted for cash. He once said, “I have heard the Buddha call body and worldly life illusion, and urge us to benefit others—had his true body remained, and the world gained from cutting it apart, he would still have it severed; how much less would he spare these copper statues?

sentences.zh: 」由是群臣皆不敢言。

translations.literal: ” Thereafter none of his ministers dared speak against it.
translations.idiomatic: ” After that none of his ministers dared object.

sentences.zh: 尝夜读书，见唐 元稹《均田图》，慨然叹曰：「此致治之本也，王者之政自此始！

translations.literal: Reading by night he came upon Tang Yuan Zhen’s Equal-Field Diagram and sighed with emotion: “This is the root of good order—royal government begins here!
translations.idiomatic: One night, reading, he came upon Tang Yuan Zhen’s Equal-Field Diagram and sighed: “Here is the root of good order—royal government begins with this!

sentences.zh: 」乃诏颁其图 法，使吏民先习知之，期以一岁，大均天下之田，其规为志意岂小哉！

translations.literal: ” He then ordered the diagram’s regulations promulgated so officials and people might learn them beforehand; within a year he meant to equalize fields throughout the realm—a scheme whose ambition was no small thing!
translations.idiomatic: ” He ordered the diagram’s rules published so officials and people could study them in advance, setting a year to equalize fields across the realm—an ambition that was anything but small!

sentences.zh: 其伐南唐， 问宰相李穀以计策；

translations.literal: When he campaigned against Southern Tang he asked Chancellor Li Gu for strategy;
translations.idiomatic: When he marched against Southern Tang he consulted Chancellor Li Gu on strategy;

sentences.zh: 后克淮南，出穀疏，使学士陶穀为赞，而盛以锦囊，尝置之 坐侧。

translations.literal: After taking Huainan he produced Gu’s memorial, had Academician Tao Gu write a eulogy, and kept it in a brocade bag at his seat.
translations.idiomatic: After Huainan fell he produced Gu’s memorial, had Academician Tao Gu compose an encomium, and kept it in a brocade pouch at his side.

sentences.zh: 其英武之材可谓雄杰，及其虚心听纳，用人不疑，岂非所谓贤主哉！

translations.literal: His martial talent was truly heroic, and his open mind in listening, his trust without doubt in appointing men—was this not what is called an enlightened ruler?
translations.idiomatic: His martial gifts were truly heroic; that he listened with an open mind and employed men without suspicion—was this not the mark of a worthy sovereign?

sentences.zh: 其北 取三关，兵不血刃，而史家犹讥其轻社稷之重，而侥幸一胜于仓卒，殊不知其料 强弱、较彼我而乘述律之殆，得不可失之机，此非明于决胜者，孰能至哉？

translations.literal: In taking the Three Passes in the north his armies scarcely drew blood, yet historians still mocked him for slighting the weight of the state and gambling on a hasty victory—little knowing he had weighed strength against weakness, compared foe with self, seized the moment when Shulü was near collapse, and grasped an opportunity not to be missed—who but one clear about decisive victory could have done this?
translations.idiomatic: In recovering the Three Passes his armies scarcely drew blood, yet historians still faulted him for gambling the altars of state on a rash stroke—never seeing that he had gauged strength and weakness, weighed foe against self, and struck when Shulü was failing, seizing a moment that would not come again. Who but a man clear in the art of decision could have done it?

sentences.zh: 诚非 史氏之所及也！

translations.literal: Truly this was beyond what mere chroniclers could reach!
translations.idiomatic: Truly the historians themselves could not have matched him!
